newsitem.title: USA: Digi Intl to concentrate on profitability.
newsitem.headline: Digi Intl to concentrate on profitability.

text.p: Digi International Inc said Thursday it would concentrate on bringing the company back to consistent profitability in fiscal 1997.

Digi, which provides data communications hardware and software, reported a first quarter loss of $0.19 a share versus a profit of $0.33 a share a year earlier. Sales were $42.24 million compared with $43.72 million.
According to First Call, the consensus of analysts' estimates for the quarter was a loss of $0.09 a share.

"Going forward, Digi will concentrate on a variety of steps which are intended to bring it back to consistent profitability, which will require a combination of actions during 1997," Jerry Dusa, acting chief executive of Digi, said in a statement.

"The company intends to simplify operations, increase consolidation, reduce expenses and manage more effectively," Dusa said. "We will concentrate our refocused efforts where we see real growth opportunities, including our OEM (original equipment manufacturer) and international channels."
Total operating expenses declined to $21.4 million in the fiscal first quarter from $23.5 million in fiscal fourth quarter, Digi said.

Earlier this month the company had warned that its revenues would be in the $42.0 million to $42.5 million range, below analysts' estimates. It said OEM sales fell because of lower year-end inventory requirements from Digi's customers.
